messages:
Sam K: Quick ask — can someone run a small continuous-batching sweep on staging? Need to understand the tradeoffs between max_batch_tokens and max_queue_ms for the 2k/8k families. Goal: keep p99 < 250ms at ~100 qps for typical doc-length workload. Please vary: max_batch_tokens [1024,2048,4096], max_queue_ms [5,10,25,50]. Keep max_concurrent_batches=8. Paste raw CSV or quick summaries. Ping @Elena and @Marta. Example config attached.

```yaml
batching:
  enabled: true
  max_batch_tokens: 2048  # variable
  max_queue_ms: 10       # variable
  max_concurrent_batches: 8
  max_inflight_tokens: 131072
```

Elena V: On it. I'll run cb-sweep jobs on staging with redwood-2k and redwood-8k variants. Clarify: use typical seq_len distribution (median 512, 95th 1500)? Or should I force 2k tokens payloads?

Sam K: Use realistic distribution (median ~512, tail up to 2k). Also run one all-long run (forced 2k) for comparison. Thx.

PerfBot: [task-scheduler] Scheduled bench cb-sweep for job id cb-176872-01 on staging. ETA ~20m.

Elena V: First quick summary (redwood-2k, realistic dist):
config,max_queue_ms,max_batch_tokens,throughput_qps,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,drop_rate
run1,5,1024,92,38,180,260,0.0
run2,10,1024,98,42,165,240,0.0
run3,25,1024,105,55,210,320,0.01
run4,5,2048,110,48,150,220,0.0
run5,10,2048,118,52,140,200,0.0  :rocket:
run6,25,2048,120,70,190,310,0.02
run7,10,4096,115,90,260,430,0.06

Notes: 2048/10 gives the best throughput/latency mix for the realistic distribution. 4096 pushes batching but increases p99 a lot and causes backpressure drops at 100 qps.

Marta G: Nice. Two quick comments: 1) I still see the old agent bug where the queue timer isn't reset when a new batch forms — add `reset_on_merge: true` in batching config to avoid prolonged small batches. 2) For the all-long run, make sure `max_inflight_tokens` is set so we don't OOM the worker. Example change:

```diff
 batching:
+  reset_on_merge: true
+  max_inflight_tokens: 131072
```

Ryan P: Small perf tip — if your workload has repeated prompt prefixes, enable prefix caching for KV entries. Also lowering kv-cache TTL during sweeps reduces noise from cold/warm cache transitions. For our redwood-2k sweep I saw ~8% latency noise with long TTLs.

Elena V: All-long run results (forced 2k seqs):
config,max_queue_ms,max_batch_tokens,throughput_qps,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,drop_rate
long-run-1,10,2048,72,110,420,620,0.03
long-run-2,25,2048,80,140,550,900,0.08
long-run-3,10,1024,60,88,480,780,0.05

Interpretation: For long sequences throughput drops (as expected). Still 2048/10 is preferable to 1024 for mixed workloads; 4096 is only good if you can tolerate high p99 for long-tail.

Sam K: Great, thanks. Action items:
- Elena: open a short PR to add defaults: `max_batch_tokens=2048`, `max_queue_ms=10`, `reset_on_merge=true`, and `max_inflight_tokens=131072` for the 2k model family in staging config.
- Marta: can you review the batching agent fix + add unit test for reset_on_merge?
- Ryan: can you add a short note about kv-cache TTL for the test harness?

Marta G: Will do review today. I'll also add a small regression test that simulates many small concurrent requests and validates queue timers.

Ryan P: I'll submit a doc snippet and update the bench-runner default to use TTL=30s for sweeps.

Sam K: Perfect. Once PRs are up, let's re-run the 2048/10 canonical check and then promote to dedicated templates. Link to perf dashboard: https://go/perf/cb-staging (internal). :eyes:

PerfBot: [task-complete] cb-176872-01 completed. Artifacts: s3://redwood-staging-bench/cb-176872-01/results.csv

Elena V: Uploaded the full CSV to the task artifact link and added a short Loom recording with pprof flame for a slow worker. Loom: https://loom.redwood/example

Sam K: Thanks team :rocket: — will follow up with a PR checklist and timeline later today.
